correctness.rationale: For all integers \(a\ge b\ge1\), the upper coloring uses the apex favorite, then b favorite available colors for B, then the last color for all A; every envy arc points backward. With \(b\ge2\), adversarial preferences ensure that after removing any apex color, each side has a distinguished witness favoring every remaining color. Nonempty disjoint used-color sets induce alternating functions between sides; a finite functional cycle gives an actual vertex envy cycle in every proper coloring using \(b+1\) colors. The \(b=1\) triangle case completes quantifiers and boundaries. Reconstructed proof and verified the standard-library package checker: zero stable colorings across six exhaustive cases and acyclic greedy colorings on 700 profiles. Enumeration is corroboration only.
